title: LIVE SURFACE CURRENTS
source_name: NOAA/NOS Great Lakes Operational Forecast System (GLOFS: LSOFS/LMHOFS/LEOFS/LOOFS) surface-current nowcast + NOAA/GLERL experimental GLCFS-FVCOM Huron-Erie Corridor & lower St. Marys River nowcast fill
variable: u_eastward / v_northward surface-layer velocity components (filed m/s, direction of water motion TOWARD); speed = sqrt(U^2+V^2), displayed in cm/s; arrows ride RK2 streamlines integrated through the filed (U,V) field, oriented by local flow
display_units: cm/s (speed gradient; arrows ride the flow)
coverage: Five Great Lakes + Mackinac Straits + upper St. Marys River (operational GLOFS) + St. Clair River / Lake St. Clair / Detroit River (experimental HEC FVCOM) + lower St. Marys River (experimental Michigan-Huron FVCOM). Narrow rivers are restored product-locally where the shared open-lake shoreline mask reads land. Documented gaps: St. Marys rapids/locks reach, Niagara Falls/gorge reach, other minor canals.
arrows: No preset lattice: jittered seeds advected downstream along RK2 streamlines (3 px steps,<=72 px paths) through the filed (U,V) field; needle glyphs chained along each path, tangent to local flow. White 1 px core + dark outline, sharp head; gentle clamped length cue 6.5 px at 0 to 9.5 px at >=50 cm/s. Rivers get denser seeds + 3x3 display smoothing of sub-pixel steps.
what: How fast the surface water is moving right now (color = speed) and which way it flows (arrows ride the current along its own paths). Covers all five Great Lakes plus the connecting rivers and channels where NOAA models provide current vectors.
why_extreme: Open-lake drift (a few cm/s, blue) owns most of the color resolution; river/channel jets to 100+ cm/s compress into red/dark-purple.
